rows.candidate_review: Separate a generic invariant from any mechanism-specific duty.
rows.context: - **Token Exchange.** A Token Exchange derivation ({{RFC8693}}) that returns only an access token establishes no new grant lineage: ordinary in-Mission delegation ({{delegation}}) and self-exchange down-scoping ({{self-exchange}}) both work this way, and the issued token is a derived token ({{mission-claim}}) whose `mission` claim identifies the one Mission its `subject_token` resolved to. Where the `subject_token` was issued under a grant lineage, the issued token retains that grant provenance, and a later redemption of a designation derived from it validates all applicable backing-grant state ({{delegated-exchange}}). A Token Exchange that instead establishes a redeemable grant lineage, such as the continuation profile's delegation-family-creating exchange ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-continuation}}), creates a new grant binding, rooted in that same Mission. Three Token Exchanges are covered by the two items below instead: cross-domain projection and child creation, which return a JWT authorization grant, and expansion, which creates a successor. - **Cross-domain projection.** A cross-domain projection ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain}}) establishes no destination-side grant binding. A Resource AS consumes the cross-domain grant, and the local access token it mints there is a derived token: it identifies the one originating Mission (`mission.id`, `mission.issuer`) but is not backed by a persistent local lineage. A Resource AS holds a destination-side grant binding only where it separately establishes a redeemable grant lineage mapped to the Mission, such as a refresh-token family. - **Child Missions and successors.** A Child Mission ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-child-delegation}}) and an expansion successor ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-expansion}}) are new Missions. Any grant binding or derived token they carry is their own under the same rules, not an extension of the origin Mission's binding. They relate to their origin only by lineage (the child's `parent` member, the successor's `predecessor` member).

Mission Lifecycle Signals ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-signals}}) specifies a Shared Signals and CAEP profile for Mission lifecycle events, delivered as Security Event Tokens ({{RFC8935}}). - **Human-in-the-loop suspension.** The base lifecycle is `active` and `terminated` ({{lifecycle}}). Mission Status ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-status}}) defines a `suspended` state with `resume`/`complete` transitions as an optional extension. A pending-human-approval state and a holding-token pause-and-resume protocol are future lifecycle work. - **Multi-hop cross-domain projection.** Cross-Domain Projection ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-domain}}) specifies a single projection hop. Mission Cross-Organizational Delegation ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-oauth-mission-cross-org-delegation}}) profiles recursive delegation across organizations; a destination verifies that delegation chain before projecting. Re-projecting a Mission from one Resource AS into a further domain is future work. - **Decentralized agent identity.** Agent identity and credentialing are out of scope ({{I-D.draft-ietf-wimse-aims}} and the WIMSE architecture, {{I-D.draft-ietf-wimse-arch}}); this document governs the approved-task artifact those identities act within, not the identities themselves. - **Cross-audience unlinkability.** A single canonical Mission Identifier lets any party holding a token correlate a Mission's activity across audiences and resources. The `authority_hash` anchor is not part of that baseline correlation surface: it stays on the Mission Record and the audit and profile surfaces that carry it by disclosure privilege ({{mission-claim}}, {{caller-authorization-and-minimization}}), not on every token by default. Pairwise or unlinkable presentation of Mission-bound authority works against the identifier and is therefore future work ({{mission-identifier-correlation}}).
